title: Account Salvage Ops Canvas + QBR Exec Brief
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational canvas + QBR-ready executive brief designed to run a fast, evidence-driven salvage sprint for accounts showing early-to-mid renewal risk. The goal is to give CSMs, AMs, AEs, and Customer Success leadership a single page of diagnostic heuristics, mitigation plays, escalation triggers, and pre-wired executive talking points so an urgent renewal can be converted into a stable relationship or an orderly offboarding with learning artifacts.

Audience:
- CSM / AM owning the account (primary)
- AE and Solutions Engineer (support)
- CS leadership (escalation)
- Finance / Rev Ops (contracting support)

Quick Canvas (one page) — fill in during initial triage (30–90 mins):
1) Signals observed (quantitative + qualitative):
   - Last 30d API calls drop: absolute and per-user (e.g., -42% total token usage; peak queries down 55%)
   - Error rate / latency regressions (incidents): service errors > 3% or sustained p95 latency > SLO
   - Feature flag changes or infra churn (deploy within 14d)
   - Support tickets open and age (tickets > 7d unresolved)
   - Exec/Champion contact frequency (dropped from weekly to none)
   - NPS/CSAT decline, renewal survey flags
2) Top 3 root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
   - H1: Product is failing to deliver key business outcome (latency/cost tradeoff)
   - H2: Internal rollout / config change caused regression (model switch, quantization mismatch)
   - H3: Procurement/budget changes or org restructure (people change)
3) Evidence to collect (minimum viable evidence):
   - Usage time series (30/90d), per-tenant cost delta, p50/p95 latency trends
   - Recent release notes / infra deploy timeline and canary logs
   - Support ticket transcripts + top-two bug repro steps
   - Contract/PO status and upcoming renewal date
4) Immediate mitigations (first 72 hours):
   - Stabilize: Pin prior model version or route to dedicated capacity; enable fallback model variant
   - Patch: Apply hotfix or rollback config within canary window
   - Customer comms: Send templated acknowledgment + 24h action plan
   - Operational: Open an incident with SRE/Infra and prioritize 1-week fix slot
5) 7–30 day plan (owner / success metric / acceptance):
   - Week 1 (CS/SE): Confirm RCA and deploy temporary mitigations (owner CSM / SE). Acceptance: usage stops dropping, error rate < 1%
   - Week 2–4 (Product/Infra): Deliver permanent fix or workflow advice; acceptance: restoration of 90% of pre-decline usage OR written agreement on phased feature roadmap
   - 30–90 day (GT/Finance): Negotiate renewal terms / proof-of-value run and commit to executive review if metrics recover
6) Exec ask (what we need from customer execs):
   - 30-minute exec sync with sponsor + CTO/Platform owner within 7 days
   - Agreement on pilot scope, success metric, and decision date

Risk Scoring Rubric (quick):
- Score 0–10 (higher = more at-risk) based on: time-to-renew (30d windows), usage decline magnitude, recent support incidents, champion engagement, contract dependency (core platform vs optional feature)
- Triage bands: 0–3 (low), 4–6 (medium), 7–8 (high), 9–10 (critical)

QBR Prep Checklist (for exec briefing slide deck):
- Slide 1: TL;DR (ask + current risk score + 1-paragraph root cause summary)
- Slide 2: Data snapshot (30/90d usage, cost delta, latency/error charts)
- Slide 3: Timeline of changes/incidents + key support threads
- Slide 4: Mitigations executed and early results (week 1 metrics)
- Slide 5: Proposed 30/90 day plan + executive asks
- Slide 6: Commercial options (standard renewal, short-term extension, pilot discount, migration assistance)
- Appendix: incident logs, ticket links, SE notes, contract summary

Renewal Tracker (columns to maintain per-at-risk account):
- Account name | Renewal window (date) | Current risk score | Main champion (name, title) | Last active contact date | 30d usage delta (%) | Open tickets (#) | Last significant deploy (date) | Current mitigation state | Next action owner | Next action date | Commercial option considered | Exec sync scheduled (Y/N)

Escalation Path & SLAs (templates below):
- CSM rapid triage: 24h to open canvas, 48h to present initial mitigation plan to customer
- SRE/Infra: 48h to accept incident and provide recovery ETA for platform faults
- CS Leadership: escalate if score >= 7 or no recovery within 7 days; leadership to join exec sync within 72h of escalation
- Rev Ops/Legal: engage for contract amendments if commercial instrument required (SLA credits, term changes)

Pre-written Templates (copy/paste-ready)
1) Customer acknowledgement (first 24h)
Subject: Account health and immediate action plan — [Account name]
Hi [Champion name],
Thanks for flagging recent issues. We’ve opened a priority incident and our team will: (1) stabilize traffic using fallback routing within 24h, (2) run a focused RCA and update in 48h, and (3) propose a short plan for the next 7 days. Can you share the best window for a 30-minute call in the next 48h?
— [CSM name]

2) Exec invite (when score >= 7)
Subject: Executive sync request — [Account name] (renewal [date])
Hi [Sponsor name],
We’d like to request a 30-minute executive sync to review recent platform behavior, proposed mitigations, and a short-term success plan to ensure your renewal path is on track. Our ask: a decision point 30 days after the sync to confirm restoration or an agreed phased roadmap. Proposed times: [three options].
Thanks,
[Head of CS]

3) AE negotiation starter (commercial options listing)
- Option A: Standard renewal (no change)
- Option B: 3-month extension + success metrics + 20% credit on overage during recovery window
- Option C: Pilot renewal (6 months) at discounted rate with milestone-based payments

Battle Cards — objection handling (CS / AE)
- "Costs spiked": show token-level breakdown, call out batching/quantization recommendations, offer short-term credits tied to success metrics
- "Latency increased": show p95 before/after, explain rollback or model pin plan and timeline; offer dedicated capacity evaluation
- "We’re moving to a competitor": ask for a 1:1 with technical champion to map feature parity and propose migration assistance with time-bound incentives

Operational Scripts (quick):
- For SE to run: reproduce steps -> gather model variant + kv-cache size + sample prompt -> capture p50/p95 -> attach to ticket
- For CSM to run: confirm champion availability -> send acknowledgement -> schedule 30m quick triage -> solicit decision maker for exec sync if score >= 7

Executive Briefing One-Pager (text block to paste into slide 1)
[Account name] — Renewal window: [date]
Risk score: [x/10]   |  Ask: 30-minute exec sync to align on pilot metrics and decision date
Top-line: Usage down X% last 30 days after [deploy/model change] leading to a mismatch with expected SLA. Immediate mitigation applied (fallback model + pinned version). Next steps: confirm 7-day stabilization; if metrics recover, proceed to standard renewal; if not, present commercial option B for phased commitment.

Metrics to include in QBR (minimum):
- Monthly active API keys / distinct users
- Total tokens and tokens per call distribution
- P50 / P95 latency by region and model
- Error rate and top-5 error codes
- Support ticket volume by severity and age

After-action & learning capture (post-resolution)
- Fill short postmortem: incident summary, root cause, mitigation timeline, what worked, what didn’t, and recommended prevention (owner + date).
- Update internal runbook: add new RCA patterns or SE debug commands that mattered
- Schedule 1:1 with product onboarding to discuss model variant selection guidance for similar customers

Minimum artifacts we require before exec sync:
- 30/90d usage chart (CSV or screenshot)
- Incident timeline and ticket links
- Cost delta analysis and any suggested billing credits
- Suggested commercial options (AE + Rev Ops sign-off)

Sample short postmortem template (to paste into Confluence):
- Title: [Account] outage / regression — [dates]
- Summary (1–2 lines):
- Impact: (users affected, revenue at risk, prod features impacted)
- Timeline: (key events)
- Root cause: (concise)
- Mitigations: (what we did)
- Action items: (owner, due date)
- Learnings & prevention

Notes / Open questions (to capture during triage):
- Who is the legal/commercial signatory and procurement cycle length?
- Any existing penalties/credits in current contract?
- Are there downstream teams relying on this integration (third-party embed, internal app)?

How to use this doc in practice:
1) CSM creates a copy of this canvas in the account folder and fills top 6 boxes within 30–60 minutes of risk flag.
2) Attach required artifacts and notify CS leadership if score >=7.
3) Run 72-hour stabilization workflow; if not successful, request exec sync and present the one-pager.
4) Use renewal tracker row to record decisions and commercial option chosen.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call SRE & SE
- Snapshot of model config and commit hash at time of regression
- KV cache metrics and memory pressure stats
- Recent quantization steps and toolchain notes
- Canary vs global deploy status

End of document.
